Although swings in net exports have affected the data, recent indicators suggest that economic activity has continued to expand at a solid pace. Given still-elevated inflation and tight labor conditions, maintaining the 4.25–4.50 percent target range with ongoing balance-sheet runoff aligns with Taylor-rule/DSGE guidance and real-time risk-management cautions about output-gap mismeasurement (Taylor; Rudebusch; Orphanides). The reliance on interest on reserves, standing repo facilities, and the ON RRP is consistent with modern corridor-system operating procedures (Goodfriend), while QT can raise term premia and influence the yield curve (Cochrane–Piazzesi)—together implying a cautiously positive but guarded tone.
